idiom_name: @Service class with constructor-injected collaborators (Kotlin constructor properties + Spring's container)
implementation_notes: Kotlin compresses the classic structure into a one-line injection target: @Service class OrderFacade(private val inventory: InventoryService, private val pricing: PricingService, private val repo: OrderRepository) - the framework autowires the single primary constructor without @Autowired, and the collaborators are read-only vals, which is the constructor-injection style the Kotlin/Spring documentation recommends over lateinit field injection. The container (Spring, or Ktor's application modules with an explicit composition root) supplies what the EJB container used to: proxy-based @Transactional demarcation, scoping and lifecycle; the class itself remains the coarse use-case boundary. Keep the explicit use-case class rather than top-level facade functions once the workflow must be transactional, shared by several entry points, or mocked in isolation.
pitfalls: Kotlin classes and members are final by default, so Spring's CGLIB proxy cannot subclass the facade and @Transactional is silently ignored unless the class is open or the kotlin-spring (all-open) plugin is applied.
As in Java, a @Transactional member invoked from inside the same class bypasses the proxy; route such calls through the injected bean instead.
lateinit var field injection compiles but hides the dependency graph and fails at runtime rather than at startup; keep the primary constructor as the only injection point.
